title: APS Registered Replication Reports: shared-protocol multi-lab replication publication rail
summary: Promotes APS Registered Replication Reports as infrastructure: a publication and coordination rail for multi-lab replications whose results should be published regardless of outcome.

status_history.note: Promoted or created in rev0012 multi-lab replication / boundary-map pass.

claims.claim: APS describes Registered Replication Reports as multi-lab direct replications using shared vetted protocols to estimate the size of an effect.
what_would_change_status: APS changes RRR description or journal policy.

evidence_refs.locator: APS page: direct replications estimate true effect size; RRR uses multiple direct replications and same vetted protocol.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: APS says well-designed replication studies should be published regardless of effect size or statistical significance, making RRRs a denominator-visibility rail for replication outcomes.
what_would_change_status: Journal policy changes or published outcomes show outcome-dependent suppression.

evidence_refs.locator: APS page: well-designed replications should be published regardless of effect size/significance.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: AMPPS RRR guidelines encourage Stage 1 submissions with commitments from at least 10 labs and use in-principle acceptance before data collection as part of the publication rail.
what_would_change_status: Guidelines change or archived policy shows different lab-count expectations.

evidence_refs.locator: Guidelines snippet: Stage 1 report, at least 10 labs encouraged, in-principle acceptance and recruitment.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

limitations: No full list of every RRR imported.
No audit of compliance with publication guarantees.

type_payload.jurisdiction_or_scope: Psychological science journals / AMPPS and APS-hosted RRR materials
reporter_protection_design: not confidential reporting; publication and protocol-commitment rail
limitations: not every replication is an RRR
publication guarantee depends on protocol compliance and journal process
type_payload.query_value: Turns a single replication attempt into a planned multi-lab estimate with ex ante protocol review and outcome-independent publication posture.

handling_notes: Avoid turning replication into researcher humiliation or field dismissal.
Preserve the difference between failed, narrowed, inconclusive, and robust effects.
Do not promote clinical, educational, or policy implications beyond the source-backed record scope.

unknowns: No full child-record extraction of each original study, lab, dataset, and author response in this revision.
No local archived copy or full line-by-line source edition yet.
Future revisions should add post-RRR/meta-analytic status histories and field/practice lag checks.
next_actions: Create child records for each included original effect where source permanence and author-response materials justify it.
Add negative controls and successful controls from additional fields.
Separate direct replication, conceptual replication, reproducibility, and generalizability claims in later records.

revision_history.change: Claim support migrated to typed evidence_refs; factual claim text and statuses unchanged.
